alternative_hypotheses: Cross-layer cost ranking identifies the best FARO layer.
contrasts_performed: A/B and Tier A against C/D across the full period.
April, May and June monthly quality density.
Ticket-status and travel-window high-intent buckets against exploratory buckets.
COMMERCIAL matched economics separated from ATTENTION and ACTIVATION.
Platform and campaign descriptive density against qualified volume.
Top ad_id_norm concentration without creative causality.

discarded_hypotheses: Volume alone is sufficient to explain quality.
Cross-layer universal KPI ranking is valid.

intermediate_findings.observation: El periodo genera 1329 leads, 397 A/B y 58 Tier A.
intermediate_findings.importance: La calidad existe, but 70.1 percent permanece en C/D; this constrains scale decisions.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Tier quality is observed lead quality, not downstream revenue or CRM value.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Tier A/B was compared against C/D with the full-period denominator.

intermediate_findings.observation: Junio concentra 776 leads y 229 A/B, pero su tasa A/B (29.5 percent) queda cerca de abril (31.0 percent).
intermediate_findings.importance: Volume grew faster than quality density; this separates scale success from structural quality improvement.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Weekly comparability and intra-month edges remain not_available in the current Evidence Set.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Monthly lead, A/B and Tier A counts were compared across April, May and June.

intermediate_findings.observation: `tiene_billetes` reaches 157 A/B from 177 leads, while `solo_mirando` reaches 48 A/B from 838 leads.
intermediate_findings.importance: The ticket-status split explains a large quality gradient and changes what Marketing should test.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: The relation is observational; causality requires a controlled experiment.
intermediate_findings.comparison: High-intent ticket-status buckets were compared against exploratory demand.

intermediate_findings.observation: `menos_de_1_mes` reaches 74 A/B from 80 leads, while `aun_no_claro` reaches 26 A/B from 463 leads.
intermediate_findings.importance: Travel-window readiness reinforces the intent explanation through an independent qualification signal.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Travel window is a lead qualification signal, not a confirmed purchase outcome.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Near travel windows were compared with unclear travel windows using A/B and Tier A density.

intermediate_findings.observation: COMMERCIAL matched links 873.650006 EUR, 1187 leads and 344 A/B.
intermediate_findings.importance: The governed direct cost-quality universe has cost per A/B of 2.5397 EUR and cost per A of 18.201 EUR.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: This economic reading applies only to the matched COMMERCIAL universe.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Matched COMMERCIAL economics were separated from layer-level spend totals.

intermediate_findings.observation: ATTENTION, ACTIVATION and COMMERCIAL carry different FARO roles and cannot be ranked as one universal efficiency table.
intermediate_findings.importance: This prevents a false optimization claim based on non-equivalent strategic layers.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Impacto asistido de ATTENTION remains UNKNOWN without downstream or assisted-effect evidence.
intermediate_findings.comparison: FARO layers were compared by governance status, not by a universal KPI hierarchy.

intermediate_findings.observation: Facebook contributes 894 leads and 278 A/B; Instagram contributes 435 leads and 119 A/B.
intermediate_findings.importance: Platform differences are visible but not strong enough to override the intent and FARO findings.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Platform is not isolated from campaign mix, ad mix or qualification intent.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Platform A/B density and Tier A counts were compared as descriptive segments.

intermediate_findings.observation: The retargeting campaign has higher A/B density than the acquisition campaign, while acquisition carries most qualified volume.
intermediate_findings.importance: This creates a volume-quality trade-off that must be handled as portfolio design, not as a simple winner/loser ranking.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Campaign interpretation is partial because ad-set and temporal spend joins are not available.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Campaigns were compared by lead volume, A/B volume, Tier A and average score.

intermediate_findings.observation: The top two ad_id_norm values concentrate 1002 leads and 288 A/B leads.
intermediate_findings.importance: Ad concentration identifies where to inspect and test, but it does not prove creative causality.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: Ad names, creative metadata and controlled creative tests are unavailable.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Top ads were ranked by lead and A/B concentration while preserving the creative-causality limit.

intermediate_findings.observation: Weekly quality, ad-set segmentation, temporal spend and ad-spend joins are absent from the current canonical Evidence Set.
intermediate_findings.importance: These missing dimensions define the boundary between current decisions and future evidence needs.
intermediate_findings.uncertainty: The absence is not filled from historical outputs or inference.
intermediate_findings.comparison: Available canonical dimensions were contrasted with baseline-pattern dimensions that remain not_available.
